items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had heard any number of Earl Hines records and there was no greater jazz piano player for me at that time

ctx.x: out their voices, and the orchestra did not have to soften their tone when Deppe sang.

I found out later that the pianist in Deppe's orchestra was a young man by the name of Earl Hines. One night Lois Deppe stopped at the Woodlawn. This Road House did not cater for negroes, but the owner would allow them to come in and say hello to the musicians if they were musicians also. A few days after the visit of Lois Deppe, Edgar Hayes announced that he was leaving to go with Deppe's orchestra who was working somewhere in Cleveland Ohio.

We certainly hated to see Edgar Hayes leave the orchestra but Deppe had offered him more money than he was making at Woodlawn Inn and Hayes wanted to go places, so we said goodbye to him and he left Cincinnati still owing me 10 dollars.
